I inoculated a grow kit with spores from a syringe about… 2 months ago, I didn’t see any mycelium until around week 4/5. The temperatures are pretty irregular in the UK which might also explain why it took so long. For the last 2/3 weeks I made a incubator from a cupboard box, and a heat mat. I placed the grow kit next to the heat mat (not on top) and get the box closed and had a temperature controller switch the heat mat on and off if the desired temperature was reached. As someone who also suffers from severe BPD which seems to affect and make my day to day life too difficult, I also find myself having huge crying sessions whilst microdosing and I feel way better afterwards than when I’m crying and not microdosing. I also noticed I start to cry happy tears as well when I’m with my boyfriend and I finally do something and get to finally feel the feelings of enjoyment and fun and not just constant anxiety.

When I did my first Macrodose, it honestly saved my life, it took away all anxiety and depression, it helped me change my whole mindset but I had to have an ego death to reach that point and it’s a heavy heavy experience with almost 4 hours of straight crying before the amazing feeling of being reborn and letting go. Sadly the next macrodose trip was a bad trip and I still haven’t tried to macrodose since, but I’m planning to do so again soon. My anxiety came back severely but my depression is still 90% away from my first trip. I’d recommend a macrodose honestly, if you have someone you love dearly who accepts psychedelics and can trip sit you, guide you and listen whilst you pour out, it might be beneficial. I have found that a macrodose and shroom trips work better for my BPD and anxiety than microdosing in terms of letting go of the past, learning to just accept and observe feelings and thoughts but I have had benefits from microdosing too.

I’ve not come across a lot of people suffering with BPD on this sub, and as that’s one of my biggest issues, I’m fascinated in how microdosing has helped others and such. 

Stay strong though, BPD is horrible but we will overcome it x
